title: Asking What a Director Sees Can Change What Vision-Language Models Choose
abstract: arXiv:2610.29318v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models are now routinely tested on theory of mind: whether they can work out what another person sees, knows, and means. A common design asks the model to report that perspective and then to act for the person, and reads a correct report beside a wrong action as a failure to use the perspective. That reading rests on a quiet assumption: that asking for the report leaves the action unchanged. We show that it does not. In a rendered Director Task, a partition hides the largest block from a director who asks for "the largest block". Asking first which blocks the director can see raises the share of replies that choose this hidden block by 12 to 88 percentage points on six GPT models and by 17 on Qwen3.8-27B, even though the models mostly report correctly which blocks the director sees. Reasoning traces and prompt rewordings suggest why: the question shifts how the request is read, from the director's view toward the model's

translated_title: 询问“导演看到了什么”可以改变视觉语言模型的选择
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型如今常被用于心智理论能力的测试：即它们能否推断出另一个人看到什么、知道什么、意指什么。一种常见的测试设计是要求模型先报告该视角，然后为该人采取行动，并将“正确的报告伴随错误的行动”解读为模型未能运用该视角。这种解读建立在一个未曾言明的假设之上：即要求报告不会改变模型的行动。我们证明事实并非如此。在一个渲染实现的导演任务中，一块隔板挡住了导演的视线，使其看不到最大的方块，而导演要求“拿最大的方块”。如果先询问模型“导演能看到哪些方块”，会使六个GPT模型选择这个被遮挡方块的比例提高12到88个百分点，Qwen3.8-27B模型提高17个百分点——即使这些模型大多能正确报告导演能看到哪些方块。推理轨迹和提示词改写实验揭示了原因：这个问题改变了模型对请求的理解方式，使其从导演的视角转向了模型自身的……
tldr: 研究发现在导演任务中，先询问视觉语言模型“导演能看到什么”会显著改变其后续行动选择（选择导演看不到的方块的比例提高12至88个百分点），这挑战了“要求报告视角不会影响行动”的传统测试假设。
en_tdlr: Asking vision-language models to first report what a director can see significantly changes their subsequent action choices in a Director Task (raising the selection of the director-invisible block by 12–88 percentage points), challenging the assumption that requesting a perspective report leaves the model's action unchanged.
